input.analysisXml: <analysis><fit>STRONG</fit><careerArcSummary>Solo IC who shipped two infrastructure migrations end-to-end (EKS controller, auth cutover), moving from individual service work toward platform-shaped ownership.</careerArcSummary></analysis>

output.stageDescription: Final round — mutual-fit / why-this-role preparation grounded in the candidate's real career arc, the JD, and research.

coachingNotes.title: Stage positioning
coachingNotes.body: Anchor why-this-role in your real career arc; ground every talking point; ask questions that prove you researched this company.

finalPrep.whyThisRole: You've shipped two infra migrations end-to-end as a solo IC — the EKS migration controller and the sessions-to-JWT auth cutover. This role's platform-team mandate is the natural next step: it takes the migration ownership you've already demonstrated and adds the scope of doing it for many service teams. That trajectory fit — not a manufactured mission story — is why this role, why now.

mutualFitTalkingPoints.point: I can own a platform migration end-to-end without a team scaffolding around me.
mutualFitTalkingPoints.grounding: Drove the EKS migration controller solo — design, build, and the dual-read cutover — cutting deploy time from 40m to under 8m.

mutualFitTalkingPoints.point: I think about cutover safety, not just the happy path.
mutualFitTalkingPoints.grounding: Ran a dual-read window during the auth sessions-to-JWT migration so the switch was reversible under load.

substantiveQuestions.question: The JD mentions you're mid-migration to EKS — is the platform team owning the cutover end-to-end, or is each service team self-serving it with platform tooling?
substantiveQuestions.rationale: Tells me whether my end-to-end migration-ownership experience maps to how you actually run platform work, or whether the role is more about building self-serve tooling.

substantiveQuestions.question: How does the platform team decide which abstractions to own versus leave to service teams — is there a written boundary, or is it negotiated case by case?
substantiveQuestions.rationale: Surfaces whether platform scope is well-defined here, which shapes how much of the role is greenfield design versus maintaining existing contracts.

finalPrep.longTermFraming: Over the next 1–3 years I want to move from owning individual migrations to owning the platform abstractions other teams build on. This role is the bridge to that, which is the honest reason I'm here — not a generic ambition to grow.
